Westerns were exactly the same. They were the most popular of genres. It allowed for testosterone driven action, scenic and/or exotic locations, conflict between good & evil, and even romance. You could tell almost any story in a Western--crime, romance, mystery, revenge, war. One of the benefits of telling these types of stories in a Western is that you can strip things down to very basic elements since you're placing the story in an agrarian society, usually in the desert regions of the American Southwest.

It should be noted that Westerns didn't really die a natural death in popular culture. As a genre, Westerns in cinema actually got bigger in the 1960s with the Italians re-inventing the entire genre and introducing the anti-hero as protagonist. And TV was replete with Westerns. In the late 60s-early 70s, however, the broadcast networks conducted what is known as the Rural Purge and cancelled nearly all Westerns and rural-based shows regardless of good ratings. This was done in order to introduce modern, urban programming. The Italians kept making Westerns intermittently through the 70s, but Italian filmmakers pursued a ton of different genres (Poliziotteschi, Giallo, horror, et.al.) so Westerns were not as frequent, good, or as popular. By the time John Wayne died in the late 70s, Hollywood Westerns were basically dead.

In many ways, Star Wars ushered in the new era of the dominant fantasy genre. And it did so by incorporating many Western motifs. Instead of an evil villain in a black cowboy hat, you've got Darth Vader. You've got the desert planet of Tatooine. You've got a gun-slinging, rogue in Han Solo. Hell, you've even got a bar scene and bar fight. I'm not arguing that Star Wars is a direct rip-off of Westerns, only pointing out how the fantasy genre incorporated much of the Western formula.

One thing that's not really been brought up by anyone else is that westerns were comparatively cheap to make.

Compared to other genres like sci-fi, horror, swords & sorcery or historical drama etc, the special effects are just guns and few explosions, there's no real make-up to worry about. The costumes are basically cowboy hats an boots, there's no cars you have to crash for stunts, the sets are easy to build (there's no palaces or castles) and filming 'on location' just means driving 30 minutes out of town to the desert/hills. The only real challenge is horses and other animals.

Making a western themed TV show was pretty cheap and didn't require actors and crew to work away from home.
